correctness.rationale: On the event every edge has at least two samples, polygon-minus-hull area is exactly a sum of m disjoint corner triangle areas (sine angle times product of nearest-edge distances divided by two). The bad event is exponentially unlikely. Simultaneous short-arc avoidance probabilities give 2m independent Exp(1) corner limits; uniform exponential tails of truncated gaps and an exponential bad-event bound establish all fixed integer moment limits. Tail integration gives the exact (N+1)(N+2) mean denominator up to exponentially small terms. Heron, sine law, and the unique positive side-product root establish the inverse, and two noncongruent isosceles triangles of equal perimeter and circumradius establish minimality. VERIFY.py was executed from its actual supplied path; it checks 480 direct area identities and 6400 high-sample trials.

value.rationale: The full limiting law distinguishes stochastic area loss from expectation-only approximation theory; it gives a natural two-moment inverse to reconstruct any triangle from a single geometric random-hull observable when perimeter is known. The explicit two-solution isosceles counterexample proves one moment insufficient; a sharp variance-to-mean-square lower bound detects equilateral geometry. The exponentially accurate universal finite-sample mean correction adds a usable quantitative approximation. The precise N² scaling, non-Gaussian product law, and inverse map are all mathematically motivated rather than arbitrary numeric slices.
